sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Vehes occurs only in cognate sets and sound-correspondence tables (pp. 133-134, 140, 154, 158, 399, 407; its data are Hooley 1971 wordlists, p. 407). No statement about Vehes stress. The only prosodic remark for the subgroup is a proto-language one (p. 157): 'Unstressed vowels were deleted or became a non-phonemic schwa (re-phonemicised in some daughter-languages) in Proto Hote/Buang, creating consonant clusters' — not a stress-placement rule for Vehes.

sources.note: No phonology content: a classification, census-division village lists and maps. The introduction explicitly declines to give phonetic values ('anything less than full phonological statements of each vernacular will, in any case, not lead to an acceptable pronunciation'). sources.note: The sole first-hand Vehes data (survey wordlist, c. 200 items) and the source behind every later citation of Vehes forms (Ross 1988, Smith 1988, ASJP). A lexicostatistical survey, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it is the only place a first-hand phonological remark on Vehes could exist.
